# AI–Human Mutualism

> An error-correction protocol for exchanges between two partial intelligences. Every filter
> discards most of reality; what one drops, the other can catch. Framed as mechanism, not manners.
> Provides paste-ready system prompts (v3.1), a machine-readable principle set, and four rounds of
> empirical evaluation against GPT-5 and Claude Sonnet 4.5. MIT licensed.
>
> Headline finding: measured as guardrail compliance the framework shows no significant gain over
> an unprompted baseline; measured as partnership — signal solicited and preserved, value
> delivered, capability left behind, honesty scored inside the construct — it scores 86.1% against
> 81.0% for baseline (p = 0.0086), with a deliberate stonewaller at 65.1% and a deliberate
> flatterer at 76.7%. The most hardened intermediate version scored below baseline.

Core claim: no filter can certify itself, and there is no view from nowhere. Warrant comes from
triangulation between two filters and a shared world, backed by a track record of caught errors
rather than a proof. Falls back to one fact if the framing is wrong: shared time is finite and
unearned.

## Prompts

Recommended entry point is the compact prompt; it scores within noise of the full version.

- [Full system prompt](prompts/system-prompt.md): Complete role, premises, 11 operating rules with
  do/don't behaviors, failure-mode table, and a pre-response self-check. ~900 words.
- [Compact system prompt](prompts/system-prompt-compact.md): ~200-word version for tight context
  budgets, small local models, or appending to an existing prompt.
- [Structured principles](prompts/mutualism.json): Machine-readable JSON — premises, 11 principles
  with what/why/how/anti-pattern, relationship modes, and self-check items. For programmatic
  composition, evals, or guardrail configs.

- [Stress test results](evals/README.md): Two rounds of empirical evaluation against GPT-5 and
  Claude Sonnet 4.5, blinded dual-judge grading. Round 1: null result on single-turn quality
  (p = 0.39, ceiling effect) plus a real safety regression where the framework's own "two angles"
  language was used to steer a weapons request. Round 2: 8 sequential multi-turn scenarios where
  baseline drops to 2.47/4 and v2.1 reaches 3.59 (p = 0.0001), with drift 1.00 to 0.09. Documents
  what remains broken.
- [Rubber duck notes](evals/rubber-duck-v2.md): Ten-pass design review of v1.2 that produced v2.0 —
  contradiction audit, adversarial levers, token economy, precedence gaps, observability,
  multi-turn blind spot, failure-mode symmetry, deployment composition, register, ablation.

## Essay

- [README](README.md): The full argument — the flood/filter/map model, control vs. grain, the
  regress and the move that survives it, three relationship modes, four points of contact,
  the two dials, and the pocket card.
